tasks.title: Derive PermissionMode from the SDK and widen every pinning site, with schema migration 6
acceptance: C1 (union derived). `<worktree>` below and in every criterion of this manifest is the session worktree root, C:/Users/dmarq/Development/Repos/orcastrate/.claude-worktrees/20261119-2021-permission-modes-from-sdk. In `src/shared/contracts/events.ts`, `PermissionMode` is a type-only alias of the `PermissionMode` exported by `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` (contract permission-modes.ts): `grep -n "export type PermissionMode" <worktree>/src/shared/contracts/events.ts` prints exactly one line, that line contains none of the mode literals ('default', 'acceptEdits', 'plan', 'bypassPermissions', 'dontAsk', 'auto'), and the alias resolves to the SDK's type, either through a type-only import of `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` in events.ts or an inline `import('@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk')` type on that line (C9 and C10 are what show it is the SDK's type and not a copy). At base (events.ts:157) the line is a four-literal union, so this fails at base.

C2 (union docblock restated). The `PermissionMode` docblock in events.ts states in place that the union is derived from the SDK, that every runtime mode list must be exact over it in both directions and fails `npm run typecheck` otherwise, names the lists that rule applies to (`ALLOWED_PERMISSION_MODES` in src/main/pod/options.ts, the schema-head list in src/main/store/schema.ts) and says `manual` stays rejected. Measured: `grep -c "are a deliberate product" <worktree>/src/shared/contracts/events.ts` prints 0 (base 1, events.ts:138, the claim that dontAsk and auto are a deliberate omission), `grep -c "Adding a fifth mode means" <worktree>/src/shared/contracts/events.ts` prints 0 (base 1, events.ts:152, a checklist naming a constant schema.ts no longer interpolates) and `grep -c "The FOUR permission modes" <worktree>/src/shared/contracts/events.ts` prints 0 (base 1). No session id and no `.sir/` path in the docblock (lessons.md 2026-11-11 rule).

C3 (allow-list contents). `ALLOWED_PERMISSION_MODES` in src/main/pod/options.ts holds exactly the contract's six modes in the contract's order, declared `as const satisfies readonly PermissionMode[]`. tests/unit/pod/options.test.ts asserts `[...ALLOWED_PERMISSION_MODES]` equals that six-element list AND that its sorted copy equals the sorted keys of a `Record<PermissionMode, true>` object literal declared in the test (the literal is what ties the count to the SDK union rather than to a number written twice). Evidence: `npx --prefix <worktree> vitest run --root <worktree> tests/unit/pod/options.test.ts` exits 0 and its RUN line names <worktree>. Fails at base (four modes).

C4 (allow-list completeness guard). options.ts carries a build-time guard that a union member missing from `ALLOWED_PERMISSION_MODES` fails typecheck, spelled through a generic `T extends never` constraint, not an empty-array assignment (contract permission-modes.ts; the vacuity of the array spelling is documented at schema.ts:96-107). Shown in C10.

C5 (runtime guard behaviour). `isAllowedPermissionMode` returns true for each of the six modes and false for 'manual', 'root', 42 and null; `createPodRunnerWith(sdk.bridge)(podOptions({ permissionMode: 'auto' }))` and the same with 'dontAsk' do not throw; `runner.setPermissionMode('auto')` forwards 'auto' to the fake SDK; 'manual' at construction and through setPermissionMode still throws /unsupported permissionMode/, and its test keeps a `@ts-expect-error` so the type rejects it too. Each is an `it` in tests/unit/pod/options.test.ts; evidence is C3's command. The negative tests that named 'dontAsk' and 'auto' as rejected (options.test.ts:78-106 at base) are gone or repointed: `grep -n "'dontAsk'" <worktree>/tests/unit/pod/options.test.ts` prints no line inside a `toBe(false)` or `toThrow` assertion.

C6 (options.ts docblock). The docblock above `ALLOWED_PERMISSION_MODES` no longer says dontAsk and auto are unexposed: `grep -c "deliberately unexposed" <worktree>/src/main/pod/options.ts` prints 0 (base 1, options.ts:26) and `grep -c "The four permission modes Orcastrate exposes" <worktree>/src/main/pod/options.ts` prints 0 (base 1, options.ts:19). It states in place that the list is exact over the SDK-derived union and that 'manual' (CLI-accepted, not in the SDK union) is rejected.

C7 (IPC validator message derived). `requirePermissionMode` in src/main/ipc/validate.ts builds its message from `ALLOWED_PERMISSION_MODES` (contract permission-modes.ts): `grep -c "default, acceptEdits, plan, bypassPermissions" <worktree>/src/main/ipc/validate.ts` prints 0 (base 1, validate.ts:76). New file tests/unit/ipc/permission-mode-validation.test.ts asserts `requirePermissionMode('manual')` throws with message exactly `permissionMode must be one of default, acceptEdits, plan, bypassPermissions, dontAsk, auto (received "manual")`, and returns its argument for each of the six. Evidence: `npx --prefix <worktree> vitest run --root <worktree> tests/unit/ipc/permission-mode-validation.test.ts` exits 0, RUN line names <worktree>.

C8 (envelope repointed). tests/unit/ipc/envelope.test.ts uses 'manual', not 'dontAsk', as its known-invalid mode: `grep -c "dontAsk" <worktree>/tests/unit/ipc/envelope.test.ts` prints 0 (base 3: :87, :89, :330), and a new `it` asserts `pod:setPermissionMode` with 'dontAsk' and with 'auto' is NOT answered INVALID_ARGUMENT (it reaches the throwing stub manager, so the code is the manager's, not validation's). Evidence: `npx --prefix <worktree> vitest run --root <worktree> tests/unit/ipc/envelope.test.ts` exits 0.

C9 (backlog check: removing a mode fails typecheck; red step, injected). Inject in src/shared/contracts/events.ts, at the `export type PermissionMode` line only, the right-hand side `Exclude<import('@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk').PermissionMode, 'auto'>` (a local copy of the union minus one mode; this text was compiled against the SDK at authoring time). Run `npm --prefix <worktree> run typecheck:node` and, separately, `npm --prefix <worktree> run typecheck:web`. Predicted: typecheck:node exits non-zero and prints at least one diagnostic line beginning `src/main/pod/options.ts(` and at least one beginning `src/main/store/schema.ts(`; typecheck:web exits non-zero and prints at least one line beginning `src/renderer/src/contracts/renderer-view.ts(`. Revert, read the line back, and report the window (injected text, both commands, the revert read-back).

C10 (adding a mode fails typecheck; red step, injected). After C9's revert is verified, inject at the same line `import('@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk').PermissionMode | 'manual'`. Predicted: `npm --prefix <worktree> run typecheck:node` exits non-zero with a TS2344 diagnostic on a line beginning `src/main/pod/options.ts(` and another beginning `src/main/store/schema.ts(`; `npm --prefix <worktree> run typecheck:web` exits non-zero with a diagnostic on a line beginning `src/renderer/src/__tests__/wording.e2e.test.tsx(`. Revert, read back, report the window.

C11 (migration 6 exists). schema.ts appends `{ version: 6, sql: MIGRATION_6 }` to `MIGRATIONS`, and `CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION` is 6. Migration 6 rebuilds `pods` (create pods_new, copy, drop, rename) with its CHECKs built only from migration-6-local pinned constants (`MIGRATION_6_PERMISSION_MODES`, six modes in the contract order, `as const satisfies readonly PermissionMode[]`; and a migration-6 pod-status list or literal), never from the live `PERMISSION_MODES`/`POD_STATUSES` (database discipline: a released migration is never edited, so per-migration lists are pinned; schema.ts:22-27). New file tests/unit/store/migration-6.test.ts asserts the version; every existing store test that pinned 5 now pins 6 or reads `CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION`.

C12 (migration 6 preserves rows). migration-6.test.ts builds a real v5 database (migrations 1-5 applied, at least two Pods one of which is a fork carrying non-null `forked_from_pod_id` and `forked_from_cc_session_id`, plus lanes and events), runs `migrate()`, and asserts the pods, lanes and events row counts are unchanged and every pods row's column values are identical before and after.

C13 (migration 6 widens the CHECK). After migration 6, a raw `UPDATE pods SET permission_mode = ?` succeeds for each of the six modes and throws /CHECK constraint failed/ for 'manual' (in migration-6.test.ts). A Pod created through the store API with permissionMode 'auto', and one with 'dontAsk', reads back with that mode from `getPod`.

C14 (named FK carried across). After migration 6 the `sql` of `pods` in `sqlite_master` contains `CONSTRAINT fk_pods_forked_from_pod_id REFERENCES pods(id) ON DELETE SET NULL` (database discipline: constraints are named explicitly), and deleting the fork's parent leaves the fork row with `forked_from_pod_id` NULL and `forked_from_cc_session_id` unchanged.

C15 (index recreated). After migration 6 `idx_pods_forked_from` exists on `pods` and its `sqlite_master.sql` equals the value read from the same database before `migrate()` (migration 5's docblock, schema.ts:727-734, says any future pods rebuild must recreate it; database discipline: every foreign key is indexed).

C16 (no data lost to the FK trap). After migration 6, `PRAGMA foreign_key_check` returns no rows, and deleting one migrated Pod removes exactly that Pod's lanes and events (counts for its pod_id go to 0, the other Pod's are unchanged), proving `lanes.pod_id` and `events.pod_id` still reference the rebuilt `pods`.

C17 (tests 12-16 can fail; injected). Separately, one at a time, each reverted and read back before the next: (a) delete the `CREATE INDEX idx_pods_forked_from` statement from MIGRATION_6 — `npx --prefix <worktree> vitest run --root <worktree> tests/unit/store/migration-6.test.ts` fails on C15's test; (b) remove the `CONSTRAINT fk_pods_forked_from_pod_id` words from MIGRATION_6's column (leaving `REFERENCES pods(id) ON DELETE SET NULL`) — the same command fails on C14's test. Report each window.

C18 (migration 3 not edited; preserved, newly tested by the existing frozen tripwire). `MIGRATION_3` and `MIGRATION_3_PERMISSION_MODES` are unedited: `grep -n -A5 "^const MIGRATION_3_PERMISSION_MODES = \[" <worktree>/src/main/store/schema.ts` prints the same six lines as at base (schema.ts:280-285: the four modes default, acceptEdits, plan, bypassPermissions and `] as const satisfies readonly PermissionMode[];`), and `npx --prefix <worktree> vitest run --root <worktree> tests/unit/store/migration-frozen.test.ts` exits 0 with its `it.for([1, 2, 3, 4])` list unchanged (it renders migration 3 from the module and compares it byte-for-byte with the blob that shipped it).

C19 (permission-mode schema-head guard re-keyed; injected). `_UncoveredAtSchemaHead` (schema.ts:331-333 at base, keyed to MIGRATION_3_PERMISSION_MODES) is keyed to `MIGRATION_6_PERMISSION_MODES` through `_AssertNever`, and its docblock says so. Inject: delete the `'auto',` element from `MIGRATION_6_PERMISSION_MODES` only. Predicted: `npm --prefix <worktree> run typecheck:node` exits non-zero with a TS2344 diagnostic on a line beginning `src/main/store/schema.ts(`. Revert, read back, report the window.

C20 (pod-status schema-head guard re-keyed; injected). `_PodStatusCoveredAtSchemaHead` (schema.ts:345-347 at base, keyed to MIGRATION_3_POD_STATUSES) is keyed to migration 6's pinned pod-status list through `_AssertNever`, so a sixth PodStatus demands a migration after 6 rather than an edit to migration 3. Inject: delete `'closed',` from migration 6's pod-status list only. Predicted: `npm --prefix <worktree> run typecheck:node` exits non-zero with a TS2344 diagnostic on a line beginning `src/main/store/schema.ts(`. Revert, read back, report the window.

C21 (live list and docblocks in schema.ts). The live `PERMISSION_MODES` holds the six modes. Migration 6's docblock, and no other docblock this task writes, carries the reversibility statement; it states in place: why a rebuild, that FK enforcement must be off around it (and that `SqliteEventStore.migrate()` provides that), that it recreates `idx_pods_forked_from` and carries both ancestry columns and the named FK, that it backfills nothing, and that it is NOT REVERSIBLE with the reason (database discipline: every migration declares reversibility). `grep -c "NOT REVERSIBLE" <worktree>/src/main/store/schema.ts` prints 5 (base 4: migrations 2-5).

C22 (store suite). Every store test that asserted 'dontAsk' or 'auto' is rejected at head (migration-2.test.ts:267, migration-3.test.ts:426, schema.test.ts:165 at base) now asserts only 'manual' is rejected, and schema.test.ts's head test accepts all six. Evidence: `npx --prefix <worktree> vitest run --root <worktree> tests/unit/store` exits 0, RUN line names <worktree>.

C23 (dialog option data). `PERMISSION_MODE_OPTIONS` in src/renderer/src/contracts/renderer-view.ts holds six entries in the contract's display order (default, acceptEdits, plan, dontAsk, auto, bypassPermissions); the four existing entries are byte-identical to base (renderer-view.ts:176-200); the dontAsk and auto entries are exactly the contract's DONT_ASK_OPTION and AUTO_OPTION. Its docblock (renderer-view.ts:162-174 at base, which still says the file does not compile until a T1 lands) is rewritten to state the exactness rule in place. wording.e2e.test.tsx asserts the display order and that the set of modes with `danger: true` is exactly ['bypassPermissions'].

C24 (exhaustive record widened). `EVERY_PERMISSION_MODE` in src/renderer/src/__tests__/wording.e2e.test.tsx (:62-67 at base, four keys) has the six keys, and its two existing tests ("holds exactly the members of the PermissionMode union" and "renders one option in the New Pod dialog per union member") pass: `npx --prefix <worktree> vitest run --root <worktree> src/renderer/src/__tests__/wording.e2e.test.tsx` exits 0, RUN line names <worktree>.

tasks.title: Cache each Pod's auto-mode support in main and push it to the renderer store
acceptance: B1 (bridge). `SdkSession` in src/main/pod/sdk-bridge.ts gains optional `supportedModels?(): Promise<unknown>`, and `defaultSdkBridge` implements it as the query's `supportedModels()` answer, unchanged. New tests/unit/pod/sdk-bridge-models.test.ts, on the precedent of tests/unit/pod/sdk-bridge-commands.test.ts (which mocks `query`), asserts a sentinel answer is resolved unchanged and the query method is called exactly once. Evidence: `npx --prefix <worktree> vitest run --root <worktree> tests/unit/pod/sdk-bridge-models.test.ts` exits 0, RUN line names <worktree> (`<worktree>` as defined in T1 C1).

B2 (runner passthrough). `PodRunner` in src/shared/contracts/pod-runner.ts gains optional `supportedModels?(): Promise<unknown>`, documented in place with the same three rules `supportedCommands` states at pod-runner.ts:327-340 (unvalidated answer; `null` when the bridge has none; NOT_RUNNING before start and after stop). New tests/unit/pod/supported-models.test.ts asserts the runner resolves the bridge's answer unchanged after start (sibling supportedCommands is tested in tests/unit/pod/supported-commands.test.ts, so the new member gets the same coverage).
B3 (runner null). The same file asserts the runner resolves `null` when its bridge's session has no `supportedModels` member.

B4 (runner NOT_RUNNING). The same file asserts `supportedModels()` rejects with a PodRunnerError of code NOT_RUNNING before `start()` and after `stop()`. Evidence for B2-B4: `npx --prefix <worktree> vitest run --root <worktree> tests/unit/pod/supported-models.test.ts tests/unit/pod/contract.test.ts` exits 0, with `EXPECTED_MEMBERS` in contract.test.ts (9 entries at base, :17-27) now also listing 'supportedModels'.

B5 (selection rule, matches). New src/main/pod-manager/auto-mode-support.ts exports a pure function (no I/O, clock or logger) that takes a session's raw `supportedModels()` answer and its latest `system`/`init` `model` (both `unknown`) and returns `boolean | undefined` by this rule: the matching entries are the object entries of the array whose `value` or `resolvedModel` strictly equals the model string; the answer is true if any matching entry has `supportsAutoMode === true`, else false if any has `supportsAutoMode === false`, else undefined. tests/unit/pod-manager/auto-mode-support.test.ts asserts: a `value` match with true gives true; a `resolvedModel` match with false gives false; two matching entries, one true and one false, give true.

B6 (selection rule, unknowns). The same test file asserts undefined for: no entry matches; the matching entry lacks `supportsAutoMode`; models is not an array; model is not a string; a non-object array entry is skipped without throwing. Evidence for B5-B6: `npx --prefix <worktree> vitest run --root <worktree> tests/unit/pod-manager/auto-mode-support.test.ts` exits 0.

B7 (rule test can fail; injected). In the rule function, change the match so it compares only `value` (drop the `resolvedModel` comparison). Predicted: B6's command fails on the resolvedModel test. Revert, read back, report the window.

B8 (manager read). After a Pod's runner starts, PodManager reads `runner.supportedModels?.()` once, NOT awaited by openPod (precedent: `#readSlashCommands`, pod-manager.ts:852-892), bounded by a named timeout constant exported from auto-mode-support.ts (backend discipline: every async call across a process boundary carries a timeout). A rejection or a timeout logs exactly one warn naming the Pod id and changes no cached value; an answer for a session disposed before it settles is dropped silently. Each is an `it` in a new tests/unit/pod-manager/auto-mode-cache.test.ts using the fakes in tests/unit/pod-manager/helpers.ts.

B9 (manager observe). PodManager reads each session's latest `system`/`init` `model` from the messages it already observes, in its own guard separate from ingest and slash commands (pod-manager.ts:1386-1400 shows the pattern), and derives the session's answer from that model and the session's models answer whenever either changes. Tested in auto-mode-cache.test.ts: a session whose models answer arrives before its first init produces no push until the init arrives; a later init with a different model re-derives.

B10 (cache and push). PodManager keeps one app-level cached value (`boolean | null`, null at construction). When a session's derived answer is defined and differs from the cached value, the cache takes it and exactly one push is sent on the new channel with payload `{ supported: <value> }`; an equal answer sends nothing; an undefined answer changes nothing; null is never pushed. The cache survives `closePod` of the Pod that produced it. Two Pods, A answering false then B answering true, produce exactly the pushes [false, true] in that order. Each is an `it` in auto-mode-cache.test.ts.

B11 (cache test can fail; injected). In PodManager, remove the 'differs from the cached value' condition so every defined answer pushes. Predicted: `npx --prefix <worktree> vitest run --root <worktree> tests/unit/pod-manager/auto-mode-cache.test.ts` fails on the equal-answer-sends-nothing test. Revert, read back, report the window.

B12 (push channel). src/shared/contracts/ipc.ts adds `EVENT_CHANNELS.autoModeSupport: 'push:autoModeSupport'`, an exported payload type `{ supported: boolean }` and `OrcastrateApi.on.autoModeSupport(cb): Unsubscribe`, each documented in place with the contract auto-mode-support.ts semantics. `Pushes` (src/main/pod-manager/pushes.ts) gains `autoModeSupport(payload)`, which `createPushes` sends on that channel; a test asserts the channel and payload (sibling push methods are tested through tests/unit/pod-manager helpers' `recordAttempts`). tests/unit/ipc/channels.test.ts pins 8 push channels (base 7, :51) and still 23 invoke channels (:45, the control: no invoke channel is added).

B13 (preload). src/preload/api.ts implements `on.autoModeSupport` by the existing `subscribe` helper, and src/preload/api.test.ts's push-subscription table (:257-290 at base) includes it, so the subscribe/deliver/unsubscribe test runs for it. Evidence: `npx --prefix <worktree> vitest run --root <worktree> src/preload/api.test.ts tests/unit/ipc/channels.test.ts` exits 0.

B14 (stub). src/renderer/src/test-utils/stub-api.ts supports `emit.autoModeSupport({ supported })` through its existing per-channel emit mechanism and delivers nothing unless emitted (contract auto-mode-support.ts `StubAutoModeSupportEmit`); stub-api.test.ts's walk over `EVENT_CHANNELS` covers it. Evidence: `npx --prefix <worktree> vitest run --root <worktree> src/renderer/src/test-utils/stub-api.test.ts` exits 0.

B15 (renderer store and hook). The workspace store subscribes to `on.autoModeSupport` in `start()` and unsubscribes in `stop()`, holds the latest pushed value (null before any push), and `useAutoModeSupport()` (declared in renderer-state.ts, implemented in workspace-provider.tsx, exported from state/index.ts) returns it without issuing any IPC call (frontend discipline: nothing is fetched in response to a render). New src/renderer/src/state/auto-mode-support.test.tsx asserts: null before any emit; false after `emit.autoModeSupport({ supported: false })`; true after a following `{ supported: true }`; and `api.calls` unchanged by rendering the hook.

B16 (store wiring pinned). workspace-provider.test.tsx's hook list (:77-95 at base) includes `useAutoModeSupport`, and its push-subscription sweep (:183-205, read off EVENT_CHANNELS) passes for the new channel. `WorkspaceStore`'s keys are unchanged: src/renderer/src/state/panel-provider.test.tsx is not edited and passes (the control). failure-paths.e2e.test.tsx pins 8 push channels (base 7, :604) and still 23 invoke channels. Evidence: `npx --prefix <worktree> vitest run --root <worktree> src/renderer/src/state src/renderer/src/__tests__/failure-paths.e2e.test.tsx` exits 0.

B17 (docblocks). Every docblock T2 adds states its rule in place; none cites a session id, a gate decision label such as `D1`, or a `.sir/` path (lessons.md 2026-11-11). Measured: `grep -rnE "\bD1\b|20261119|\.sir/" <worktree>/src/main/pod-manager <worktree>/src/main/pod <worktree>/src/shared/contracts <worktree>/src/renderer/src/state <worktree>/src/renderer/src/contracts <worktree>/src/preload` prints nothing (base: prints nothing; positive control: the same pattern run on C:/Users/dmarq/Development/Repos/orcastrate/.sir/sessions/20261119-2021-permission-modes-from-sdk/contracts/auto-mode-support.ts prints at least one line).

B18 (green at this task's tip). `npm --prefix <worktree> run typecheck` exits 0, and `npm --prefix <worktree> test` exits 0 with its RUN line naming <worktree>, run after B7's and B11's reverts are verified.

tasks.title: New Pod dialog offers all six modes and hides auto when the cached flag is false
acceptance: F1 (wiring). PodsChrome reads `useAutoModeSupport()` (contract auto-mode-support.ts) and passes it to NewPodDialog as an internal prop `autoModeSupported: boolean | null` declared on `NewPodDialogInternalProps` in NewPodDialog.tsx (internal props are the component's own, renderer-view.ts header; `NewPodDialogProps` is not changed). NewPodDialog calls no hook from `../state` and never reaches the preload bridge (frontend discipline: presentation components take data and callbacks).

F2 (nothing cached shows six; backlog check). With `autoModeSupported` null, the dialog renders exactly six mode radios, one per key of a `Record<PermissionMode, true>` literal in NewPodDialog.test.tsx, each found by `testId(TEST_IDS.newPodModeOption, mode)`. `<worktree>` as defined in T1 C1. Evidence: `npx --prefix <worktree> vitest run --root <worktree> src/renderer/src/pods/NewPodDialog.test.tsx` exits 0, RUN line names <worktree>. (Satisfied by NewPodDialog.test.tsx at T1's tip only through the array; this criterion requires the record-keyed test.)
F3 (true shows six). With `autoModeSupported` true, the same six radios render (a test in NewPodDialog.test.tsx).

F4 (false hides auto only). With `autoModeSupported` false, exactly five radios render, there is no element with test id `new-pod-mode:auto`, and the other five are present (a test in NewPodDialog.test.tsx).

F5 (hidden selection reverts). With `autoModeSupported` null, select auto; rerender with false: the auto radio is gone, the default radio is checked, and submitting a valid draft calls `onCreate` with `permissionMode: 'default'`. The visible list is computed from `PERMISSION_MODE_OPTIONS` and the prop on each render, not stored (frontend discipline: derived values are computed, never stored): `grep -c "useState(\|useState<" <worktree>/src/renderer/src/pods/NewPodDialog.tsx` prints 7, the base count.

F6 (new modes submit). With `autoModeSupported` null, a valid draft with auto selected calls `onCreate` with `permissionMode: 'auto'`, and one with dontAsk selected calls it with `permissionMode: 'dontAsk'`; neither selection shows the bypass warning (`TEST_IDS.newPodBypassWarning` absent) nor disables Create (danger stays on bypassPermissions only).

F7 (hiding test can fail; injected). In NewPodDialog.tsx, make the visible list ignore `autoModeSupported` (render every entry of PERMISSION_MODE_OPTIONS). Predicted: F2's command fails on F4's test and on F5's test. Revert, read back, report the window.

F8 (end to end through the store). New src/renderer/src/__tests__/auto-mode-option.e2e.test.tsx mounts the workspace with `stubOrcastrateApi()` via `mountWorkspace` from src/renderer/src/__tests__/harness.tsx, emits `autoModeSupport({ supported: false })`, opens the New Pod dialog by `TEST_IDS.newPodButton`, and finds no `new-pod-mode:auto` but finds `new-pod-mode:dontAsk`. Evidence: `npx --prefix <worktree> vitest run --root <worktree> src/renderer/src/__tests__/auto-mode-option.e2e.test.tsx` exits 0.
F9 (end to end, true). The same file emits `{ supported: false }` then `{ supported: true }` before opening the dialog and finds `new-pod-mode:auto`.

F10 (no session pointers anywhere; repo-wide, DAG tail). `grep -rlE "\.sir/|20261119-2021" <worktree>/src <worktree>/tests` prints nothing (base: nothing; positive control: the same command on C:/Users/dmarq/Development/Repos/orcastrate/.sir/lessons.md prints that path) (lessons.md 2026-11-11: docblocks state rules in place).
F11 (repo-wide typecheck, DAG tail). `npm --prefix <worktree> run typecheck` exits 0 (both typecheck:node and typecheck:web print no diagnostic), run after F7's revert is verified.
F12 (full suite, DAG tail). `npm --prefix <worktree> test` exits 0 and its RUN line names <worktree>, run after F7's revert is verified.
